text.p: Transmedia Network Inc said Thursday it has finalized its agreement to sell $33 million in food and beverage credits that had been purchased from restaurants for resale to members.
The agreement is part of a revolving securitization.

The credits, also called "rights-to-receive," were sold to a limited liability company, which, in turn, has issued $33 million of fixed rate securities in a private placement to institutional investors.

"The securitization of the company's 'rights-to-receive' is a breakthrough achievement for the company as it allows us to expand with a source of capital which is inexpensive, creates no debt on our balance sheet, nor does it dilute shareholder's equity," Transmedia Chairman and Chief Executive Melvin Chasen said in a statement.
The placement agent, SPP Hambro & Co, agreed to sell the entire five-year issue to one investor on November 7, Transmedia Network said.

Structured Finance Advisors, an investment advisory firm, purchased the entire issue on behalf of a group of institutional investors at 150 basis points over five-year U.S. Treasury notes, or 7.4 percent.
Transmedia said the percentage is at least 125 basis points less than it would have paid by selling notes in a traditional private placement that would have encumbered the balance sheet.
Transmedia also retains a residual interest in the anticipated future excess cash flows, which will be generated as the rights-to-receive are used by its cardmembers.

Transmedia is a membership-based company that issues a charge card designed to provide members with a convenient way to save on the purchase of a variety of products and services such as restaurants, hotels, airlines, catalogs, and other recreational facilities.
